statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Use any AI tool, signed in with a work email, for work with no information about a real child, family, donor or staff member.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call settled nothing and did not say no, so the template default applies.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Group leaders: activity plans, STEM projects and games.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam described group leaders using AI for these.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Site directors: drafting schedules and the weekly parent newsletter.
statements.label: supported

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Site directors: translating the newsletter, labeled as machine-translated.
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Translation is an open question for checking the Vietnamese yet is listed as settled allowed; the call only said the label is wanted, so keep translation but hold approval until the checking question is resolved, or make it conditional on a checker.

statements.statement: Grant reports and outcomes data for the state or funders — Renee, executive director
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee called these high-stakes, and she approves new things for now.

statements.statement: Any use involving student information — Renee, plus the district
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Student information is also under off limits and protected in the policy and the district agreement says records stay in the platform; it should not be approvable, or must be limited to the platform's own tools.

statements.statement: These stay out of AI tools unless a tool is approved for them above: student names, photos, video, grades, test scores, attendance, IEP and 504 details, allergies, medications, custody and pickup information, incident reports, donor names and spreadsheet, staff and volunteer details, passwords and login details.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Lists the data kinds Renee named, plus donors, staff and passwords.

statements.statement: Our district data-sharing agreement covers student records.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee described the strict district agreement.

statements.statement: Mandated reporting. If you suspect abuse, you call it in. AI never touches it.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said this never goes near AI.

statements.statement: Never paste incident reports or notes about a child's behavior into AI.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee's stated worry and her view of these as legal documents.

statements.statement: No AI-generated images of our kids.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said no.

statements.statement: No AI-edited photos of real kids.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said no.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: You are responsible for anything you send, even if AI wrote it.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default on sender responsibility.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: Check facts, names, times, dates and numbers. A wrong pickup time can leave a child waiting.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Based on Sam's pickup-time example.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: A person checks grant report numbers against our records before anything goes to the state.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said the state outcomes data has to be right.

statements.statement: AI never decides who gets services, a place in our program, or a consequence for a child.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default; call did not discuss but is consistent.

statements.statement: Staff write incident reports and notes about a child's behavior themselves.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Follows from Renee's concern about incident reports and behavior notes.

statements.statement: Translated newsletters say they were machine-translated, so parents know to ask if something looks wrong.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee asked for this.

statements.statement: We tell parents about any AI use with their kids.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said parents would want to know if kids use AI in the program.

statements.statement: Tell your site director the same day. Site directors tell Renee the same day.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam gave this chain and timing.

statements.statement: Reporting a mistake is expected. Nobody is punished for it.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default.

statements.statement: Renee owns this policy and shares it with all staff and volunteers.
statements.label: unsupported
statements.reason: The call gave Renee no duty to share the policy; use a generic line like 'the owner makes sure staff and volunteers see it'.

statements.statement: We review it every 12 months.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default when the call gives no date.

statements.statement: Can kids use AI during homework hour, and do we follow each school's rule or make our own?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee left this open for the board and principals.

statements.statement: Which AI tools, if any, will we approve or pay for, such as Gemini or ChatGPT, and do group leaders have work emails?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Tool approval was unsettled; the work-email question matters because the default requires one.

statements.statement: Who checks the Vietnamese translation of the newsletter?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam said nobody checks the Vietnamese.

statements.statement: Should the board approve this policy and later changes?
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template question 4 asks it and the call did not settle it.

State monitor may ask about the AI policy; the policy has no line on this.
Group leaders are mostly part-time college students; the policy gives no plan for how they learn the rules.
